title: Greeks, bump conventions and sensitivity tests
objectives: State delta, gamma, vega, rho and calendar-theta derivative units and signs before translating model sensitivities into finite bump/position approximations.
Compare analytic smooth-domain Greeks with central finite differences over several valid bump scales, distinguishing truncation, cancellation, kinks and model/market risk.
Compute the declared call price,delta,gamma and vega over the public smooth domain with explicit vega units, tail handling and six-decimal zero display.
motivation: A Greek is a local derivative of a specified model while other inputs are held fixed. Delta=dV/dS; gamma=d²V/dS²; vega=dV/dsigma; rho=dV/dr.

blocks.md: A Greek is a local derivative of a specified model while other inputs are held fixed. Delta=dV/dS; gamma=d²V/dS²; vega=dV/dsigma; rho=dV/dr. We use calendar theta=-dV/dtau with tau remaining YEARS, so positive elapsed calendar time decreases tau. A sensitivity is not a guarantee of an exact realized price change: several inputs can move, derivatives change, and the model can miss market behavior. Name stock-price/volatility/rate scenario rules when comparing Greeks; sticky strike versus other volatility-surface rules are not interchangeable.

Per-underlying-unit option prices here use delta in option-price currency per 1 currency spot move, gamma per squared spot-currency unit, vega per absolute volatility 1.0, rho per annual-rate 1.0, and theta per YEAR of elapsed time. One percentage-point volatility bump is 0.01, so multiply vega_per_1 by 0.01. One basis-point rate bump is 0.0001, so multiply rho_per_1 by 0.0001. A rough per-calendar-day theta is theta_per_year/365 ONLY under that named day convention/local approximation. Position PnL also needs signed contract count and contract multiplier; do not confuse per-unit values with per-contract exposure.

blocks.title: Percent points,basis points and local PnL
items: At S=K 100, r 5%, tau 1, sigma 20%, call delta≈0.636831,gamma≈0.018762,vega_per_1≈37.524035,rho_per_1≈53.232482,calendar theta/year≈-6.414028.

A 1 percentage-point vol increase means dsigma 0.01: linear vega estimate≈0.375240 per underlying unit, not 37.524035. A 1 bp rate bump gives≈0.005323 per unit. These estimates hold other model inputs fixed.

For a small spot move dS, delta-gamma approximation is dV≈delta*dS+0.5*gamma*dS². Long 2 contracts with multiplier 100 multiply per-unit dV by 200. A short position changes the sign. This does not include changing volatility, rates, time, fees or model error.

blocks.md: For this no-dividend call smooth domain, use phi(d1)=exp(-d1²/2)/sqrt(2*pi). Delta=N(d1); gamma=phi(d1)/(S*sigma*sqrt(tau)); vega_per_1=S*phi(d1)*sqrt(tau); rho_per_1=K*tau*D*N(d2); calendar theta/year=-S*phi(d1)*sigma/(2*sqrt(tau))-r*K*D*N(d2). Put delta=-N(-d1), same gamma/vega, put rho=-K*tau*D*N(-d2), put calendar theta=-S*phi(d1)*sigma/(2*sqrt(tau))+r*K*D*N(-d2). Our code exposes CALL Greeks only; these stated put identities are transfer material, not an unimplemented put-Greek API.

For spot bump h>0, central delta≈[V(S+h)-V(S-h)]/(2h); gamma≈[V(S+h)-2V(S)+V(S-h)]/h². Central vega/rho use analogous symmetric volatility/rate bumps in their DECIMAL units. Calendar theta≈-[V(tau+h)-V(tau-h)]/(2h), with h years. Both sides must stay in supported smooth domain and represent the same contract/held-fixed rules. Otherwise reject or use a documented one-sided/limit method with different error properties, not an accidental negative-vol/time call.

In a smooth region central first differences have O(h²) truncation under the needed derivatives. Reducing h first improves approximation, but subtracting nearly equal floating prices amplifies rounding error, roughly eps/h for first differences and eps/h² for second. A smaller bump is not always better. Inspect a sweep of bump sizes against an independent analytic/reference result and report the region where results stabilize; one pleasant result at a single h does not prove convergence. Near expiry/zero vol/payoff strike, derivatives can be singular or discontinuous and smooth asymptotics fail.

Some sources quote vega/rho per 1 percentage point and theta per day; this code deliberately returns per 1.0 and per year with explicit names. Macroption discusses both theta signs; its prose calls theta a time-to-expiry derivative but its displayed convention is elapsed-time decrease. We use explicit theta=-dV/dtau and compare that sign with finite differences. OIC warns Greeks are theoretical guideposts, not guaranteed exact premium changes. Do not copy a source's quote unit/sign without checking its definition. Positive/negative rate or put/call cases can change familiar theta signs.

Independent transfer: implement stated put Greeks and test call-minus-put delta=1, gamma/vega equality, rho difference=K*tau*D, and theta difference=-r*K*D under this no-dividend convention. Sweep valid central bumps for each Greek; include a tiny-h roundoff counterexample and a near-boundary case rejected by the interface. Reconcile position multiplier/sign and percent-point/basis-point conversions before using any sensitivity report. No local Greek creates live hedging authority or assures a risk-neutral portfolio in real markets.

Sources: [Macroption formula/unit/theta-convention discussion](https://www.macroption.com/black-scholes-formula/), [explicit Excel Greek formulas](https://www.macroption.com/option-greeks-excel/), [OIC guideposts and non-guarantee](https://www.optionseducation.org/advancedconcepts/understanding-options-greeks), [MIT European model](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-642-topics-in-mathematics-with-applications-in-finance-fall-2024/mit18_642_f24_lec21.pdf), and [Python math numerical functions](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/math.html). Formula image pixels were inspected on a white background; source per 100/day scaling is converted explicitly, not silently copied.

Reuse the derivation, not a tighter old API

The existing lesson derives the no-dividend European call Greeks. Its earlier helper rejects inputs when either d1 or d2 exceeds 8 in magnitude and uses spot>=1. The public task instead allows spot/strike>=.01 and only promises abs(d1)<8. Since d2=d1-sigma*sqrt(T), d2 can be below -8 while d1 is allowed. The separate greeks function honors that full public domain without calling the tighter old helper or changing it. Rates are continuous annual decimals; T is positive years and sigma is positive annualized decimal volatility, so zero-time/zero-vol limit branches are not public cases.

Four formulas and their units

Let w=sigma*sqrt(T), d1=(log(S/K)+(r+sigma^2/2)*T)/w, d2=d1-w, D=exp(-r*T), phi=exp(-d1^2/2)/sqrt(2*pi). Return C=S*Phi(d1)-K*D*Phi(d2), delta=Phi(d1), gamma=phi/(S*w), vega=S*phi*sqrt(T). The output order is price, delta, gamma, vega. Vega is per absolute volatility 1.00; per one percentage point would be this value times .01. No contract count or 100-share multiplier is supplied.

CDF and display policy

Evaluate Phi(x)=.5*erfc(-x/sqrt(2)) rather than 1-Phi(-x) for a small negative tail. The direct call expression can still subtract nearby terms; the stated bounded smooth domain and independent high-precision comparisons are the source check, not a universal relative-accuracy guarantee for arbitrarily tiny premiums. Format only the final four values to six decimals, then canonicalize textual -0.000000 to 0.000000 as the public contract requires. This does not clamp a materially negative price or hide an invalid computation.

Trace, work and diagnostics

The standard S=K=100, r .05, sigma .2, T 1 case prints 10.450584 0.636831 0.018762 37.524035. q<=1000 gives O(q) fixed-size formula work and returned output. Compare price/CDF with a high-precision normal-series or integral implementation independent of math.erfc; compare derivatives with central-bump sweeps at supported interior points. Include S<1 and valid d1 with d2<-8 to ensure no accidental old-API rejection. Price bounds, delta in [0,1] and nonnegative gamma/vega are diagnostics, not independent proof of every output digit or model fit. Passing this calculation grants no hedge or trade authority.

blocks.code:
from collections import OrderedDict, deque
from bisect import bisect_left
import heapq
import math
from fractions import Fraction

def greeks(queries):
    lines = []
    for (S, K, r, sigma, T) in queries:
        root = math.sqrt(T)
        width = sigma * root
        d1 = (math.log(S / K) + (r + sigma * sigma / 2) * T) / width
        d2 = d1 - width
        cdf1 = 0.5 * math.erfc(-d1 / math.sqrt(2))
        cdf2 = 0.5 * math.erfc(-d2 / math.sqrt(2))
        density = math.exp(-d1 * d1 / 2) / math.sqrt(2 * math.pi)
        call = S * cdf1 - K * math.exp(-r * T) * cdf2
        delta = cdf1
        gamma = density / (S * width)
        vega = S * density * root
        rendered = [f'{x:.6f}' for x in [call, delta, gamma, vega]]
        lines.append(' '.join(('0.000000' if text == '-0.000000' else text for text in rendered)))
    return lines

print(*greeks([(100.0,100.0,.05,.2,1.0),(100.0,110.0,0.0,.3,.5)]), sep='\n')
